claims.text: WMoTaNb high-entropy-alloy powders can be densified using spark plasma sintering.
Spark plasma sintering can retain the initial microstructure of WMoTaNb powder.
Adding 3–5 wt% Cu during powder synthesis will promote in situ formation of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates.
Sintering near 1200°C followed by heat treatment near 900°C will produce uniformly dispersed, coherent Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in WMoTaNb.
The Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will act as high-conductivity bridges in the HEA matrix.
Copper has an intrinsic thermal conductivity of approximately 400 W/mK.
Nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates will create continuous pathways for phonon and electron heat transport through WMoTaNb.
Coherent nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracking.
Coherent Cu-rich precipitate interfaces will minimize dislocation nucleation.
The Cu-rich precipitates will maintain the integrity of WMoTaNb grain boundaries.
Cu doping will increase the thermal conductivity of WMoTaNb by at least approximately 20% relative to an undoped control.
The Cu-doped alloy will retain yield strength comparable to the undoped alloy under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The Cu-doped alloy will retain ductility comparable to the undoped alloy under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Undoped tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys provide adequate mechanical strength.
Current undoped WMoTaNb intermediate layers have limited heat-transfer enhancement.
The predicted thermal and mechanical benefits will persist during cycling from room temperature to approximately 1000°C and under representative dynamic mechanical loads.
Processing optimization can mitigate precipitate coarsening and phase instability during extended high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Prolonged thermal cycling or irradiation may cause Cu-rich precipitate coarsening or phase segregation that diminishes thermal and mechanical performance.
